Toyota's entry into car manufacturing unfolded across several milestones. According to Wikipedia [d3], the history of Toyota started in 1933 when an automotive division of Toyoda Automatic Loom Works was established "devoted to the production of cars" under Kiichiro Toyoda. By 1934, the division had produced its first Type A Engine, which powered the first Model A1 passenger car in May 1935 and the G1 truck in August 1935 [d3][d9]. Toyota's official newsroom confirms that "Toyota's very first cars, the Model G1 truck, was produced by the Automotive Production Division of Toyoda Automatic Loom Works, Ltd. in August 1935" [d9]. Full production of the first production car, the Model AA sedan, began in 1936 [d1][d6], as confirmed by both Toyota UK and Britannica. Finally, Toyota Motor Company was formally incorporated as an independent company on August 28, 1937 [d7][d1][d6], marking the birth of the standalone automaker we know today.
